_brendon_hanson_: After 11 days of war, U-F19 had a place for everything. On Day 11, the men rearranged a shelf to make a place for Ulrich Hanson. The Hegemony took Grey Mill, and the orders at U-F19 changed before the cheering ended. Ulrich Hanson shouldered another load.
A patient apologized for bleeding on Ulrich Hanson's sleeve. He told the patient to concentrate on staying awake.
Ulrich Hanson started keeping a diary in the back of a field service book. First entry: "Still here."

A bullet went into Ulrich Hanson's chest just under the heart at U-F19. The medic said not to give him water, and then said nothing more. Shot by Anselm Ofsoup of the Concord (@sea_ofsoup). Ulrich Hanson did not last the night outside the full aid post. The bearers who carried him in carried him out again at dawn.
The papers say Roland "Ash" Hanson. The sergeant says he has his father's eyes. Ulrich Hanson's eyes. Nobody in U-F19 argues.
Benedikt "Mole" Olliedav (Concord) and Roland "Ash" Hanson (Hegemony) watched each other through the same loophole at Lantern Hill for an hour. Neither fired. Neither will explain why.

A burst of machine-gun fire caught Roland "Ash" Hanson in the open at U-F19. The tourniquet held. Whether he holds is another matter. Shot by Otto "Spark" Kraljmk of the Concord (@kraljmk87). A rifle cracked from the far side of no man's land. Roland "Ash" Hanson fell at U-F19 and never moved again. Shot by Otto "Spark" Kraljmk of the Concord (@kraljmk87).
Otto "Mole" Hanson asked about Roland "Ash" Hanson on arriving at U-F19. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. He asked for another.

A sniper's bullet hit Otto "Mole" Hanson at U-F19. The medics worked on him in the bottom of the trench and shouted for a stretcher. Shot by Clement Realjospence of the Concord (@realjospence). Otto "Mole" Hanson stood up to fix a loose sandbag at U-F19. He did not get to finish the job. Shot by Clement Realjospence of the Concord (@realjospence).
Bram Hanson took the same post at U-F19 where Otto "Mole" Hanson stood. He found his older brother's initials carved in the wall and put his own beneath them.
A bullet bounced off the trench wall and caught Bram across the shin at U-F19. It bled a lot and meant very little. Shot by Isidor "Saint" Michael of the Concord (@john.michael2877).
abioticsquare0: Marek Abioticsquar arrived with the Day 14 draft, carrying a book with the last pages torn out and the news from home, which was old by the time he told it.
Marek Abioticsquar pressed his ear to the tunnel wall under the Chalk Pits and heard it: tapping. Someone is digging toward him.

Part of the parapet collapsed near Marek Abioticsquar. Repairs started as soon as the dust settled, with one man on watch while the rest worked. The letter for Marek Abioticsquar had been in the rain somewhere along the way. Marek Abioticsquar dried it by the stove, page by page.

Marek Abioticsquar lent Dorian Sidequests a pencil. It came back wrapped in a scrap of paper that said 'One good turn'. Marek Abioticsquar read the letter, folded it, unfolded it, and read it again. The sentry pretended not to see.

Marek took charge of the squad at W-F11 when the Private fell. By morning, the squad had a new Lance Corporal. The mail bag came up with the soup. There was a letter for Marek, and the soup went cold while Marek read it.
arthur_baker00: By the time Clement Baker reached P-F11, the war was 10 days old and had its own habits. He learned the first one within the hour: keep your head down.

Clement Baker and Roland Serreno tried to invent a new card game. The rules only made sense once they stopped betting tobacco. Grey Mill is in Hegemony hands. Clement Baker watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
Clement Baker measured the remaining pencil against the remaining paper. For once, the supplies seemed likely to run out together.
Fog so thick that Clement Baker could not see the end of his own rifle. Somewhere out there, someone was whistling.
A bullet hit Clement Baker's belt buckle at P-F11 and glanced off into his side. Shallow, the medic said. He is keeping the buckle. Shot by Albin "Doc" Stefmichael of the Concord (@stefmichael_96).

Clement Baker was found at the bottom of the trench at P-F11, hit in the head, helmet split open. He is breathing in short, loud gasps. Shot by Zeno "Bones" Teeganblair of the Concord (@teeganblair). A man in the hospital dugout died before dawn, and his bed went to Clement Baker. Nobody pretends that is not how it works. Clement Baker ate a whole bowl of soup today. The surgeon says that is better than any medicine.
Clement Baker wrote half a letter home from bed, then tore it up. It said he was fine. It was not a convincing lie.
Every bed was taken and every medic was busy. Clement Baker died waiting. The men at P-F11 have not stopped talking about it.
Albin Baker asked about Clement Baker on arriving at P-F11. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. He asked for another.
A bullet nicked Albin's boot at P-F11. The heel is gone. So is a little skin. Shot by Leopold "Crow" Napoleon of the Concord (@shooter.conqueror_napoleon).
ba_roman98: The sergeant gave Silas "Tin" Roman a dead man's blanket and a living man's job. That is how replacements start, on Day 9 or any other.
After the loss of Blackwater Canal, Silas "Tin" Roman helped stack spare sandbags at T-F3. Nobody asked when they would be needed.

Silas "Tin" Roman (Concord) and Zeno Helldiver (Hegemony) ended up in the same shell hole at Grey Mill. They stared at each other. Then each crawled home, and neither has told anyone. The Hegemony took Grey Mill. Silas "Tin" Roman watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.
Silas "Tin" Roman owes Bastian "Spark" Horton so many cigarettes that they stopped counting and started writing it down. The notebook is nearly full.
Silas "Tin" Roman fired at the enemy dawn watch from T-F3. Viktor Derpstera was badly wounded, and the enemy line spent the morning with its heads down.
The east wind brought the smell of the other trenches: smoke, lime and somebody's cooking. Silas "Tin" Roman was hungry and furious about it.
Silas "Tin" Roman reads Edmund Swag's letters from home out loud, because Edmund never learned to read. Tin leaves out the sad parts. Edmund knows.
A round went through the rim of Silas "Tin" Roman's helmet and nicked his ear on the way out. He has a notch in both now. Shot by Leopold "Parson" Carlosm of the Hegemony (@carlosm.jr).

Silas "Tin" Roman took a bullet through the hand and another through the forearm at T-F3, seconds apart. The bearers carried him back with the arm held up like a flag. Shot by Silas "Spark" Tallas of the Hegemony (@tallas154). Outside the aid post, Silas "Tin" Roman lies on a stretcher among the others. The orderlies step over him and say soon.
Silas returned to T-F3 thinner and paler, with a wound that closed without a single night in a bed. The medics count it as one of theirs.
dax_j_king: The draft reached R-F2 on Day 4. Dietrich "Tin" King was shown which board tipped, which roof leaked and which promises to ignore.
Rain all night. Dietrich "Tin" King bailed water out of R-F2 with a helmet until his hands stopped feeling anything.

Dietrich "Tin" King took a wrong turn at two identical trench junctions. He decided the route needed names that could be remembered under pressure. Dietrich "Tin" King walked the captured trenches of Hill 304 and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
Dietrich "Tin" King marked the first junction with a spoon and the second with a boot sole. Other runners have begun using the names in their directions.
Dietrich "Tin" King borrowed a book with three readers already waiting in line. For once, everyone was impatient about something harmless.
The last of the jam was shared by scraping it onto a biscuit. Dietrich "Tin" King approved the method.
Someone removed the spoon from Dietrich "Tin" King's junction to eat supper. He retrieved it and nailed it above comfortable reaching height.
The Hegemony flag went up over Blackwater Canal. Dietrich "Tin" King did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.

A round went through the rim of Dietrich "Tin" King's helmet and nicked his ear on the way out. He has a notch in both now. Shot by Pavel Rvmn of the Concord (@____rvmn). The clerk counted the names twice. Dietrich "Tin" King is number 289 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand. On Day 11, Grey Mill passed to the Hegemony. Dietrich "Tin" King wrote the name in his diary with unusual care.
The medics cleaned Dietrich "Tin" King's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at R-F2.
A new runner delivered a message using Spoon Corner and Boot Turn without hesitation. Dietrich "Tin" King drew both markers on the official route sketch.
Dietrich "Tin" King checked the safety catch three times before handing over the post. The man taking over noticed, and checked it once more.
Dietrich "Tin" King began a chess game by post with a friend at home. He copied the opening move onto the corner of an ordinary letter.
Dietrich "Tin" King spent an hour repairing a pocket. Nothing goes in it now without a careful inspection.
The reply to Dietrich "Tin" King's chess move arrived with a long complaint about the weather at home and a note that his opponent had taken a pawn.
Dietrich asked the dugout for advice on the next move. Three men disagreed so fiercely that a second board had to be drawn.
emory.mod: Marek "Smokes" Mod arrived on Day 6 as a replacement. The men in R-S7 had been fighting for 5 days already and looked at his clean boots like a rumour from another world.
Marek "Smokes" Mod measured the remaining pencil against the remaining paper. For once, the supplies seemed likely to run out together.
Marek "Smokes" Mod and Clement Breadcrumb carved a chessboard into an ammunition box. The pieces are bullets, buttons and one very patient beetle.
A muddy dog crawled into R-S7 through the wire. Marek "Smokes" Mod gave it half his bread. It has not left his side since. The men call it Kaiser.
Kaiser has learned to carry messages in a tin on its collar. Marek "Smokes" Mod is very proud. Kaiser is mainly proud of the biscuits.
News of the loss of Blackwater Canal reached R-S7 with the rations. Marek "Smokes" Mod ate while listening to the revised orders.

A parcel arrived tied with blue ribbon. Marek "Smokes" Mod gave the contents away and kept the ribbon to mark a page. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Marek "Smokes" Mod is number 424. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech. The Hegemony took Grey Mill. Marek "Smokes" Mod watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.
Marek "Smokes" Mod borrowed a serial novel from a newspaper bundle. The instalment ends with a locked door and a pistol shot. The next issue is missing.
Marek "Smokes" Mod repaired a collapsed wall of the trench at R-S7 with sandbags, boards and language not fit for letters home.
A bullet grazed Marek "Smokes" Mod's ribs at R-S7. He found the hole in his coat first and the wound second. Shot by Ulrich "Bones" Swan of the Hegemony (@swan.72041943).
The medics cleaned Marek "Smokes" Mod's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at R-S7.
Marek "Smokes" Mod has asked three carrying parties for the next instalment. So far, the search has produced racing results and an advertisement for boots.
Marek "Smokes" Mod delivered an urgent message and waited while the officer searched every pocket for a pencil to sign for it.
The dugout has begun inventing endings to Marek's story. The cook's version involves an inheritance; the corporal's involves a disciplinary hearing.
halfire87: Day 10. The corporal put Valentin Halfire beside a veteran and said to copy everything except the language.

Someone asked Valentin Halfire to wake them in ten minutes. He had no watch, so he counted slowly and woke them at what felt like ten. Day 11. The Hegemony took Grey Mill. From the heights Valentin Halfire could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.
Valentin Halfire (Hegemony) and Isidor Waylon (Concord) came to the same broken well at Lantern Hill at night, each with a bucket. They filled them in turns and backed away.
A newspaper reached Valentin Halfire with the corner torn off. According to the half a sentence that survived, the war was going well.
Valentin Halfire lent Gustav Bobopomaranc a razor. It came back sharper, with a new handle carved from an old tent peg.
Valentin Halfire found a clean spot on the table and set his bread on it. Within a minute, someone asked to borrow the spot.
Valentin Halfire and Gideon "Bones" Carnahanwile carried a kettle through three narrow turns without spilling a drop. The applause at the end caused the accident.
Valentin Halfire saw a hare run the whole length of no man's land and nobody on either side fired at it.
Valentin's left boot has opened at the toe. He tied it with string and walked as if nothing had happened.
harveyjackwoods: Lucien Harveyjackwo walked into M-F11 on Day 17 and asked where the war was. A shell answered before anyone else could.
A shot from across the wire took the top off Lucien's mess tin at M-F11. His wrist stung for an hour. Dinner was ruined. Shot by Marek "Smokes" Mcconne of the Concord (@tyler_mcconne_ll).
iago_curi: Lucien Curi introduced himself as a coal miner from Tannenfeld. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.

Lucien Curi found an old shopping list inside a coat pocket. Soap, lamp oil, apples. He folded it along the original creases. Mail came up the line with a letter for Lucien Curi. Lucien Curi read it in the dugout and kept the envelope. The Hegemony hold Grey Mill now, and they can see straight into P-F20. Lucien Curi has learned to walk bent double.

Lucien Curi let three easy targets go by. The fourth was the one worth the risk. Emil "Ash" Theteeternot was grazed. Mail came up the line with a letter for Lucien Curi. Lucien Curi read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Lucien Curi found a photograph in the mud of no man's land: a woman in a white dress, and a name on the back that is not from his side of the wire. Mail came up the line with a letter for Lucien Curi. Lucien Curi read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
A dummy head on a stick drew the enemy's eye at P-F20. Lucien Curi saw where the answering shot came from and fired back. Nils King was gravely wounded.
Lucien Curi was on wiring party in no man's land. Every time a flare went up he froze like a scarecrow. It worked.

Nobody heard the Hegemony raiders cut the wire. Lucien Curi only heard boots on the duckboards at P-F20, then nothing but pain. Raider: Casimir Eclark of the Hegemony (@eclark43). Lucien Curi went over with the night raiders, found the enemy trench empty at that spot, and came back with a bag of their biscuits.

The medic looked at Lucien Curi's wound, sniffed it, and sent him back to P-F20. Clean, said the medic. It is the best word a medic knows. A letter for Lucien Curi said the whole street was asking about the front. Lucien Curi did not know where to begin the answer.
Lucien keeps the photograph in his pocket next to a stub of a pencil. He says he will give it back after the war. Nobody asks to whom.
m0nster_boi: Otto Boi stepped off the supply cart at S-C14 and stood very still, listening to the guns as if they were saying his name.
The Hegemony secured Blackwater Canal. Otto Boi helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that he had heard correctly.

Otto Boi carried hot tea up to the front line in petrol cans. Everyone could taste the petrol. Everyone drank it. The company read out the roll of the First Thousand at the dawn watch. Otto Boi answered to number 966. Otto Boi walked the captured trenches of Grey Mill and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
Otto Boi had a letter from home. He read it four times and then once more out loud, for the men who never get any.
A lice inspection interrupted a heated argument about politics. Otto Boi pointed out that at least one enemy had been positively identified.
Otto Boi had Tobias Connordavids of the Concord in the sights at Sorrow Copse for a long second. Tobias Connordavids was lighting a pipe. Otto Boi let the match burn all the way down.
Otto Boi learned that a crate of officers' wine is stored in the cellar at battalion headquarters. He has been making careful drawings.
The cook's fire went out. Otto Boi relit it under his own coat and served stew that tasted of wool.
Otto Boi volunteered for a supply run to headquarters. He came back with exactly what was ordered and a suspiciously large coat.
Otto gave a new recruit a wooden spoon with a small carving on the handle. 'So you do not lose it,' he said.
maxhuntertattoos: Dorian Maxhuntertat arrived with the evening ration party, carrying a cracked shaving mirror and a borrowed coat two sizes too big.

Konrad "Crow" Dinhdong (Hegemony) and Dorian Maxhuntertat (Concord) spotted the same abandoned cart near Sorrow Copse. A long exchange of shots left the cart exactly where it was. The snipers took Dorian Maxhuntertat in on a busy morning in S-S4. By noon he had learned the first rule of the job, and by evening the second.

Dorian Maxhuntertat fired at the flash of a shovel across the wire. Behind the shovel was Otto "Parson" Vicious, now badly wounded. After the loss of Blackwater Canal, Dorian Maxhuntertat helped stack spare sandbags at S-S4. Nobody asked when they would be needed. A letter from home found Dorian Maxhuntertat before the night shift. Dorian Maxhuntertat folded it small and kept it close.

The cook's stew tasted of iron and smoke. Dorian Maxhuntertat ate two helpings anyway. Dorian Maxhuntertat got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 523. The men who came later will ask about it. The Hegemony won Grey Mill. In S-S4, Dorian Maxhuntertat listened to three explanations and trusted none of them.

Dorian Maxhuntertat felt a hard tug at his hip at S-S4. The bullet had cut through his belt and the skin under it. He tied the belt back together with string. Shot by Zeno Emperornoble of the Hegemony (@emperornoblez).
Dorian Maxhuntertat no longer winces when he lifts his rifle. The medic signed him off with a grunt.
Dorian Maxhuntertat noticed a loophole that had been dark for days. He watched it until dusk and wrote down what changed.

Dorian Maxhuntertat fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Quentin Elo, grazed. Nobody nearby said anything. A letter from home found Dorian Maxhuntertat before the night shift. Dorian Maxhuntertat folded it small and kept it close.

A round came through the loophole Dorian Maxhuntertat was watching at S-S4 and hit him in the collarbone. He is alive and very angry. Shot by Oskar Londonz of the Hegemony (@londonz_29). A letter for Dorian Maxhuntertat came with a photograph. Dorian Maxhuntertat looked at it for a long time and said nothing.

Dorian Maxhuntertat stopped talking around midday. The medic took one look and called for a stretcher. An orderly waved the bearers in: one bed, cleared and scrubbed. Dorian Maxhuntertat was lifted onto it in the hospital dugout.

Dorian ate a whole bowl of soup today. The surgeon says that is better than any medicine. The letter for Dorian was addressed to the wrong trench and had been to two others first. It was slightly muddy and entirely welcome.
oreo_boi_5000: Ivo Boi signed the papers with a steady hand. The trench at S-F3 took him in like it takes everyone: without a word.
Ivo Boi ended a letter with 'nothing to report', then added half a page about the missing soap.

Quentin Souptime (Hegemony) and Ivo Boi (Concord) spotted the same abandoned cart near the Drowned Farm. A long exchange of shots left the cart exactly where it was. After the loss of Hill 304, Ivo Boi helped stack spare sandbags at S-F3. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
Zeno "Lucky" Hackermt (Hegemony) and Ivo Boi (Concord) ended up in the same shell hole at Verdel Ridge. They stared at each other. Then each crawled home, and neither has told anyone.
The patrol came back one man at a time. Ivo Boi held the gap open and counted until the corporal said that was everyone.

A round came through the loophole Ivo Boi was watching at S-F3 and hit him in the collarbone. He is alive and very angry. Shot by Benedikt "Smokes" Lfer of the Hegemony (@w0lfer2210). Ivo Boi was killed outright at S-F3, a single bullet from across the wire. Shot by Benedikt "Smokes" Lfer of the Hegemony (@w0lfer2210).
Lucien Boi joined S-F3 under the shadow of Ivo Boi's name. At the first roll call, the corporal used the right one.
Lucien Boi caught a falling mug with his boot. Nobody could say if it was skill or luck, and he did not say either.
News of the loss of Blackwater Canal reached S-F3 with the rations. Lucien Boi ate while listening to the revised orders.

Lucien Boi learned that the colonel's ham is stored in the cellar at battalion headquarters. He has been making careful drawings. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Lucien Boi is number 292. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech. Grey Mill is lost. Lucien Boi heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.
Lucien Boi received the rank of Lance Corporal and a stack of unfinished paperwork. The congratulations lasted less time than the paperwork.
Lucien Boi volunteered for a supply run to headquarters. He came back with exactly what was ordered and a suspiciously large coat.

Shell splinters caught Lucien Boi in the chest and belly at S-F3. The medic worked with both hands and shouted for a bed. Lucien Boi died at S-F3 under a direct hit. A medic who saw it says it was over in a moment.
Another member of the House of Boi reached the line: Marek Boi. He asked where Lucien Boi had slept, then chose a different corner.
Across the wire at Sorrow Copse, Nils Toro of the Hegemony held up a sign: 'How is your coffee?' Marek Boi of the Concord held up a sign back: 'Worse than yours.'
Marek Boi fired, worked the bolt, and fired again. Across the wire, Rafael "Parson" Olo was gravely wounded. Marek Boi ate breakfast without a word.

Marek Boi fired at the muzzle flash across the wire before it faded. Benedikt "Mole" Fuentes was badly wounded, and that rifle did not fire again tonight. The sergeant at S-F3 called out a range and a spot. Marek Boi was the only one who hit it. Oskar Londonz was gravely wounded.
Marek found an old shopping list inside a coat pocket. Soap, lamp oil, apples. He folded it along the original creases.
rmr7015: Dietrich Rmr came up the line with a book with the last pages torn out and nothing else. The sergeant wrote him down as Private and pointed at the mud.
After the loss of Blackwater Canal, Dietrich Rmr helped stack spare sandbags at T-F17. Nobody asked when they would be needed.

Dietrich Rmr saw shapes coming through the gap in the wire and fired along it. The shapes went to ground. One of them was Isidor "Spark" Hand, grazed. News of the loss of Grey Mill reached T-F17 with the rations. Dietrich Rmr ate while listening to the revised orders.

Dawn watch. Dietrich Rmr put a round across no man's land and the enemy line went quiet: Isidor "Spark" Hand, gravely wounded. Dietrich Rmr bought War Bonds for the front. The quartermaster pinned the ribbon on personally: 'The front remembers who kept it fed.' A German shepherd wandered in from no man's land at dawn, wet and hungry. It chose Dietrich Rmr. Dietrich Rmr gave it a name: Bully.

Albin "Mole" Bricky and Dietrich Rmr both swear they saw a ghost at the Hanging Bridge. Each says the other screamed first. Dietrich Rmr gave Bully a bath in a shell hole. The dog came out muddier than before and very happy.
Out on the wire with the wiring party. Dietrich Rmr tore his hands on the barbs and did not make a sound. The new wire at T-F17 is up.
Dietrich Rmr swept the enemy parapet at T-F17 with one long burst. Dust jumped all along the sandbags. Rafael Andi was grazed.
Dietrich Rmr agreed to sit for a portrait drawn by a man with a piece of charcoal. The first result made him look twice his age.
Dietrich Rmr did not want to shoot today. Then the enemy shot first, and Dietrich Rmr fired back. Lucien Thanbrown was grazed.
Dietrich had a clear view down the enemy trench for the space of one breath. It was enough. Konrad Uselesmagika was gravely wounded.
some_random_helldiver: Day 4: Rafael Helldiver reached R-F1 with a full packet of cigarettes. Learning everyone's name proved remarkably easy.

Rafael Helldiver watched a pale shape beyond the wire while a flare burned out. It turned out to be a sack, right where the sack had always been. A letter from home found Rafael Helldiver before the night shift. Rafael Helldiver folded it small and kept it close.

Out on the wire with the wiring party. A bullet found Rafael Helldiver at R-F1, high in the shoulder. He went down hard and stayed down. A letter from home found Rafael Helldiver before the night shift. Rafael Helldiver folded it small and kept it close. Hill 304 is in Hegemony hands. Rafael Helldiver watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
Rafael Helldiver died on a stretcher outside the aid post, still waiting for a bed. The medics had nothing left to give him.
A letter came with Zeno Helldiver: "I am Rafael Helldiver's father. I have come to finish what he started." Nobody had the heart to tell him it never finishes.

A pump handle snapped off in Zeno Helldiver's hands. He fixed it while the water rose around his ankles. Zeno Helldiver transferred to the stretcher bearers. The men in R-F1 said they would miss him. He is only three dugouts away.

The company barber offered a choice of haircuts. Zeno Helldiver asked to see the second one. The barber laughed. A letter from home found Zeno Helldiver before the night shift. Zeno Helldiver folded it small and kept it close.

Zeno Helldiver offered a spare button for a better place near the stove. The offer was refused with surprising dignity. A letter from home found Zeno Helldiver before the night shift. Zeno Helldiver folded it small and kept it close.

The raiders came over the parapet in the dark. Zeno Helldiver was hit hard in the fight at R-F1 before anyone could fire. The raider was Dietrich Ripvanwinkle of the Concord. Raider: Dietrich Ripvanwinkle of the Concord (@ripvanwinkle3031). No rifles, only shovels and knives. Zeno Helldiver dropped into the Concord trench by a dugout door and met Dorian Joebandilla coming out. It was over in seconds. (@joebandilla) The flare went up just as Zeno Helldiver reached the Concord parapet. Zeno Helldiver jumped down first. Pavel "Parson" Collins was the man waiting there, and Pavel "Parson" Collins fell. (@forgettable_collins) The Hegemony flag went up over Blackwater Canal. Zeno Helldiver did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again. A letter from home found Zeno Helldiver before the night shift. Zeno Helldiver folded it small and kept it close.

Back on the fire step at R-F1. Zeno Helldiver says the wound itches, which the medics say is a good sign. A letter from home found Zeno Helldiver before the night shift. Zeno Helldiver folded it small and kept it close. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Zeno Helldiver is number 316. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech. The report confirmed the Hegemony victory at Grey Mill. Zeno Helldiver folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.

Zeno Helldiver had a letter from home. He read it four times and then once more out loud, for the men who never get any. A letter from home found Zeno Helldiver before the night shift. Zeno Helldiver folded it small and kept it close.
Zeno Helldiver was made Lance Corporal. He celebrated by sleeping four hours in a row.

The bread was divided with a ruler. Zeno Helldiver received the smallest piece and the job of looking after the ruler. Now serving as a field cook, Zeno Helldiver discovered that being experienced at the front did not prevent being new at the job.
Zeno Helldiver and Anselm Romanbhassel carried a kettle through three narrow turns without spilling a drop. The applause at the end caused the accident.

In the dark of the Concord trench Zeno Helldiver hit Severin Joebandilla with a trench club, then ran for the wire before the flares went up. (@joebandilla) The Concord sentry, Otto Collins, shouted once. Zeno Helldiver silenced the shout with the flat of a shovel and was back over the parapet a minute later. (@forgettable_collins) Zeno Helldiver went over with the night raiders, found the enemy trench empty at that spot, and came back with a bag of their biscuits.
Zeno Helldiver tried to remember the price of a loaf in Greyhallow. Three different answers seemed right, depending on how far back he thought.
Zeno ate Oskar Kirov's portion by mistake and spent the rest of the day apologizing in tobacco.
tylerjohnlaster: By the time Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas reached S-S8, the war was 5 days old and had its own habits. He learned the first one within the hour: keep your head down.

The cook's stew tasted of iron and smoke. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas ate two helpings anyway. The chaplains took Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas in on a busy morning in S-S8. By noon he had learned the first rule of the job, and by evening the second.

Zeno "Lucky" Hackermt had Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas of the Concord in the sights at Hill 304 for a long second. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas was lighting a pipe. Zeno "Lucky" Hackermt let the match burn all the way down. A letter from home found Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas before the night shift. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas folded it small and kept it close.

Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas spent an hour repairing a pocket. Nothing goes in it now without a careful inspection. A letter from home found Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas before the night shift. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas folded it small and kept it close.

Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas dreamt he was back in Saint-Lune, working as a fisherman. He woke up and said nothing all morning. A letter from home found Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas before the night shift. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas folded it small and kept it close.

Night raid. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas crossed no man's land, saw the enemy sentry too late to reach, and came back without a scratch. Next time, says Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas. Day 10: Blackwater Canal was lost. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas wrote down the news without trying to explain it. A letter from home found Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas before the night shift. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas folded it small and kept it close.

Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas held a service in a shell hole. Eleven men came. Two of them had never prayed before. Both of them asked for another. The clerk counted the names twice. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas is number 377 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand. Grey Mill is lost. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas heard the news from a runner, said nothing, and checked his rifle twice. There will be another race.
A round went through Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas's water bottle and into his thigh, but not far. He is more upset about the water. Shot by Zeno Ghostoftheas of the Hegemony (@ghostoftheast).

The medic looked at Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas's wound, sniffed it, and sent him back to S-S8. Clean, said the medic. It is the best word a medic knows. A letter from home found Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas before the night shift. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas folded it small and kept it close.

A round went through the rim of Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas's helmet and nicked his ear on the way out. He has a notch in both now. Shot by Matthias "Saint" Mulletoperat of the Hegemony (@mulletoperator). A letter from home found Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas before the night shift. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas folded it small and kept it close.

The medic cut the last bandage off Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas's arm and threw it in the stove. He went back to S-S8 the same hour. A letter from home found Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas before the night shift. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas folded it small and kept it close.

Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas drew the street leading to Saint-Lune. There was no room left for the last house, so he turned the page over. A letter for Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas came with a photograph. Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas looked at it for a long time and said nothing.
Cyril "Mole" Tylerjohnlas won a pocket watch that does not work at cards from a lance corporal in S-S8. The lance corporal wants a rematch.
Rematch. Cyril lost everything he won, plus a book with the last pages torn out. The whole dugout watched.
vandahinten: Gustav Vandahinten arrived on Day 10 and found the section asleep. The welcome had to wait until somebody needed the kettle.

Gustav Vandahinten was hit in the foot through his boot at P-F15. The boot had to be cut off. He asked them to save the other one. Shot by Otto Lopez of the Concord (@manny_lopez.18). The bearers reached Gustav Vandahinten at P-F15 too late. One shot, and it was over. Shot by Otto Lopez of the Concord (@manny_lopez.18).

The House of Vandahinten sent Tobias Vandahinten after Gustav Vandahinten. This time the family packed two pairs of spare socks. Tobias Vandahinten left the work of a sniper to become a rifleman. Someone from the old section came over to see how it was going. Grey Mill has been won. Tobias Vandahinten listened as the corporal read the news twice, once for the men just off watch.

A new recruit would not eat with the others. Tobias Vandahinten left a place at the end of the bench and said nothing about it. A letter from home found Tobias Vandahinten before the night shift. Tobias Vandahinten folded it small and kept it close.

A round went through the rim of Tobias Vandahinten's helmet and nicked his ear on the way out. He has a notch in both now. Shot by Benedikt Yeoj of the Concord (@__yeoj__). A letter from home found Tobias Vandahinten before the night shift. Tobias Vandahinten folded it small and kept it close.

Out on the wire with the wiring party. Tobias Vandahinten was hit in the forearm at P-F15. Clean through the meat, the medic said. He asked if that was good. The medic said it was the best kind. A letter from home found Tobias Vandahinten before the night shift. Tobias Vandahinten folded it small and kept it close.

Tobias Vandahinten came back to the squad today. The men had kept his spot on the fire step and his spoon. A letter from home found Tobias Vandahinten before the night shift. Tobias Vandahinten folded it small and kept it close.

Tobias Vandahinten came back from the night raid on two stretcher poles. Nobody is sure which side fired the shot. Mail came up the line with a letter for Tobias Vandahinten. Tobias Vandahinten read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Tobias Vandahinten took a bullet through the hand and another through the forearm at P-F15, seconds apart. The bearers carried him back with the arm held up like a flag. Shot by Ivo Ursarte of the Concord (@not_ursarte). Tobias Vandahinten was killed at P-F15 while passing a message along the trench. He never finished the sentence. Shot by Ivo Ursarte of the Concord (@not_ursarte).
Another member of the House of Vandahinten reached the line: Gideon Vandahinten. He asked where Tobias Vandahinten had slept, then chose a different corner.

Gideon was hit twice in the leg at P-F15. The medic cut the trouser open with scissors and said nothing useful. Shot by Isidor Gallianrecon of the Concord (@gallianrecon). The mail sergeant held up an envelope and shouted a name. It was Gideon. The whole trench clapped.
waylon_h29: Isidor Waylon reported to S-R16 with a photograph gone soft at the edges sewn into his tunic lining. The sergeant pretended not to notice.
The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal. Isidor Waylon watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.

The order named Isidor Waylon as Lance Corporal. He read it twice, then asked who would take over his watch. A thousand names now stand in the regimental book. Isidor Waylon is number 964. The sergeant pinned the ribbon of the First Thousand on without a speech. News of the loss of Grey Mill reached S-R16 with the rations. Isidor Waylon ate while listening to the revised orders.
Isidor Waylon wrote letters for men who could not write, and some for men who could but did not know the words.

Isidor Waylon was hit in the hand while passing a mug along the trench at S-R16. He did not spill a drop. The men are still talking about that. Shot by Casimir "Whistle" Chrisoostuiz of the Hegemony (@chrisoostuizen).
The medic cut the last bandage off Isidor Waylon's arm and threw it in the stove. He went back to S-R16 the same hour.

The men at S-R16 heard Isidor Waylon call out once and then go quiet. They found him hit in the back, still holding the rifle. Shot by Jonas Nicolassuess of the Hegemony (@nicolassuess). Isidor Waylon was carried into the hospital dugout feet first, because that was the only way the stretcher fit through the door.
Isidor Waylon died in the ward while the orderly was reading him a letter from home. The orderly finished the letter anyway.
The papers connected Dietrich Waylon to Isidor Waylon. The men took longer to learn Dietrich Waylon's own habits, but they made the effort.

The men at S-R16 heard Dietrich Waylon call out once and then go quiet. They found him hit in the back, still holding the rifle. Shot by Quentin "Hollow" Broadshoulde of the Hegemony (@broadshoulderedbastard). A single shot at S-R16. Dietrich Waylon sat down against the trench wall as if to rest, and did not get up. Shot by Quentin "Hollow" Broadshoulde of the Hegemony (@broadshoulderedbastard).
Clement Waylon took the same post at S-R16 where Dietrich Waylon stood. He found his cousin's initials carved in the wall and put his own beneath them.
The company barber offered a choice of haircuts. Clement asked to see the second one. The barber laughed.
yaboypolarbear: Teodor Yaboypolarbe came from Rosenau, where there is a river, a church and no mud at all. He talks about all three as if they were people.
Number 89 on the early rolls: Teodor Yaboypolarbe. The First Wave ribbon arrived with instructions about where to sew it and no needle.
Teodor Yaboypolarbe got a letter from Ilse. Two pages, one of them only about the weather back home. He read that page most.

Teodor Yaboypolarbe wrote back to Ilse and tore it up three times. The fourth version says almost nothing, which is how he knows it is the right one. Victory at Verdel Ridge. Teodor Yaboypolarbe let himself talk about leave for the first time in days. Orders assigned Teodor Yaboypolarbe to work as a rifleman. The first lesson began with what not to touch. Teodor Yaboypolarbe became a signaller today. He wrote the change in a letter home, then crossed out the explanation and tried again.
A parcel from home held a comb. Teodor Yaboypolarbe has hardly any hair left after the last haircut, but he appreciated the thought.
A bucket appeared above the Hegemony parapet at the Hanging Bridge. Teodor Yaboypolarbe fired. Gideon Bao pulled the bucket down. Later a sign went up: 'Water costs enough already.'

Teodor Yaboypolarbe spent the night filling sandbags. By dawn he could no longer close his hands. By noon the shells had emptied half of them again. A letter from home found Teodor Yaboypolarbe before the night shift. Teodor Yaboypolarbe folded it small and kept it close. The report confirmed that the Hegemony held Hill 304. Teodor Yaboypolarbe read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.

Teodor Yaboypolarbe got a photo of the family house. He spent longer looking at the strange curtains than at the faces. A letter from home found Teodor Yaboypolarbe before the night shift. Teodor Yaboypolarbe folded it small and kept it close.

A newspaper reached Teodor Yaboypolarbe with the corner torn off. According to the half a sentence that survived, the war was going well. A letter from home found Teodor Yaboypolarbe before the night shift. Teodor Yaboypolarbe folded it small and kept it close.

The corporal found out Teodor Yaboypolarbe used to be a tram conductor. Teodor Yaboypolarbe has been doing two jobs ever since. A letter from home found Teodor Yaboypolarbe before the night shift. Teodor Yaboypolarbe folded it small and kept it close.
Teodor Yaboypolarbe of the Concord spotted Emil Galvanooooo of the Hegemony repairing a parapet at the Ossuary Wood. A warning shot stopped the repair on the spot.

The Hegemony won Blackwater Canal. In R-F14, Teodor Yaboypolarbe listened to three explanations and trusted none of them. A letter from home found Teodor Yaboypolarbe before the night shift. Teodor Yaboypolarbe folded it small and kept it close.

A parcel came for Teodor Yaboypolarbe that was really meant for another soldier with the same surname. Inside: two knitted scarves. He put everything back and kept only the wrapping. A letter from home found Teodor Yaboypolarbe before the night shift. Teodor Yaboypolarbe folded it small and kept it close. Day 11: Grey Mill was lost. Teodor Yaboypolarbe wrote down the news without trying to explain it.

The men have learned that Teodor Yaboypolarbe keeps feeding the rats. Tonight it made them laugh, which was worth a great deal. A letter from home found Teodor Yaboypolarbe before the night shift. Teodor Yaboypolarbe folded it small and kept it close.
The parcel's address was smudged. Teodor Yaboypolarbe took it to the clerk, who found two possible units and no reason to hurry.
Teodor Yaboypolarbe tried to write home with gloves on. The address is readable. Everything else will need some imagination.
Teodor Yaboypolarbe dreamt he was back in Rosenau, working as a tram conductor. He woke up and said nothing all morning.

The Hegemony raiders came over at R-F14 in the middle of the night. Teodor Yaboypolarbe met them first and did not survive the fight. Killed in the night raid by Casimir Jcsv of the Hegemony (@jcsv2305).
Oskar Yaboypolarbe came to the front because his brother Teodor Yaboypolarbe never came home. He carries a child's drawing of a horse.

A single shot from across the wire hit Oskar Yaboypolarbe in the thigh at R-F14. He crawled the last yards on his elbows. Shot by Leopold Kapitancray of the Hegemony (@kapitancray). The bearers reached Oskar Yaboypolarbe at R-F14 too late. One shot, and it was over. Shot by Leopold Kapitancray of the Hegemony (@kapitancray).
The House of Yaboypolarbe sent another. Felix "Lucky" Yaboypolarbe, father of Oskar Yaboypolarbe, arrived with the same eyes and the same stubborn silence.
Pavel Guyy woke Felix from a nightmare by calling Lucky name. Felix did not say thank you, but poured the tea.
